_README: Our crop ids -> the FAO-56 rows the season calendar reads (data/crop_stages.json).
A NAMING map, not agronomy: it says which published row is about our crop.
t11 = Table 11 crop name (stage lengths); t12 = [Table 12 crop, variant or null] (Kc).
'note' is printed with the calendar wherever the published row is about a
related crop rather than exactly ours (e.g. FAO-56 publishes bell pepper).
Annual crops only: a fruit tree's year runs from its own phenology, not from a
planting date, and needs a different assembly. A crop with no t11 here, or
whose rows all fail src/season.py's checks, gets no calendar - and is told so.
TREES ('kind': 'tree') are dated from the farmer's season START, not a planting:
Table 11's 'Plant Date' for a tree is the month its year begins. Only rows
published for the Mediterranean are used, so apple, cherry, peach, grape and
walnut have none - their rows are for 'High/Low/Mid Latitudes', which FAO-56
never defines - and olive's row is the page's '2705 days' typo.
't12_range' names several Table 12 crops whose rows are printed as one range
(citrus by ground cover and canopy); 'variants' pairs each Table 11 row with
its own Table 12 row (banana's first and second year).
SPRING CEREALS come from FAO-56's one latitude-band row, 'Barley/Oats/Wheat,
March/Apr, 35-45 °L': src/season.py reads a band only when it holds all of
Türkiye. A variant's own 'note' is printed when that variant's row is used.
Barley lists the barley-naming row first: for an April planting both it and
'Grains (small)' fit, and the first in the list wins the tie.
